editorial.headline: Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali: Retail Machinery Under KBLI 47791
editorial.standfirst: This broad machinery-retail activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks its registration there today.
editorial.body:
This activity covers the retail sale of a wide field of machinery, its equipment, components and spare parts. Its agricultural range includes tractors and equipment for ploughing, fertilising, sowing, planting, mowing, spraying, peeling and threshing, as well as rice-milling units and milking machines. The same retail scope extends to hand- and foot-operated sewing machines, electric sewing machines, overlock, embroidery and oversum machines, alongside generators, welding machines, coffee and flour grinders, saws, lathes, turbines, waterwheels, looms, knitting machines and printing machines.

The appropriate registrant is therefore a business engaged in retailing these kinds of machines and their related equipment or parts, rather than a business defined by one narrow machine category. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That breadth is commercially meaningful, but it also matters to the regulatory reading: the Bali finding in this record turns on the risk treatment at the Besar scale.

Nationally, the position is clear. The PMA status is TERBUKA and the national maximum foreign ownership is 100%, meaning a foreign investor may hold the entire foreign-owned stake nationally. Bali, however, produces a different practical result. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk treatment is Low or Medium-Low across every scope recorded for this activity. Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities from PMA registration. The result is a Bali status of Blocked (risk class): a PMA investor cannot register this activity in Bali today.

That distinction is the essential one for a founder to retain. National openness and a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling remain the national position; they do not override the Bali registration block. For this particular retail activity, the machinery catalogue is expansive and the national PMA position is fully open, but Bali’s moratorium is decisive where a PMA registration in the province is concerned.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness at 100% does not make this activity registrable for PMA in Bali today.
